and it would not affect repositories with existing data. I would opt for changing the prefix mapping (in a new commit) and removing the "breaking change" label on this ticket.
An updated PR that removes the "breaking-change" nature of this ticket would be great.
The namespaces defined in the Fedora CND should be reviewed, especially test: and fedoraconfig:

In particular, the test: namespace prefix seems like an unnecessary testing artifact that is present in production deployments. Furthermore the fedoraconfig: namespace points to a non-existent URL. It may be much better to remove the test: prefix and use a non-dereferenceable namespace for fedoraconfig: (i.e. <info:fedoraconfig/>)

comments.body: Is the suggestion to replace the occurrences of the "test" namespace with something else where it is currently in use throughout tests?
Andrew Woods this PR replaces instances of the test: namespace with fedoraconfig: and removes test: entirely from the CND

I am not convinced that this is necessarily a breaking change. If a user has been using the fedoraconfig namespace prefix, then yes, it will be a breaking change, but we can simply choose a different prefix, i.e. config or repositoryconfig or repoconfig or fedoraconf and it would not affect repositories with existing data. I would opt for changing the prefix mapping (in a new commit) and removing the "breaking change" label on this ticket.

An updated PR that removes the "breaking-change" nature of this ticket would be great.
